events.title: Explorer La Salle Is Murdered in Texas
events.description: French explorer René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle, was searching for the mouth of the Mississippi River. His expedition ended in mutiny, and some of his own men killed him in what is now Texas.
events.significance: His death ended France's most ambitious attempt to plant a colony on the Gulf Coast. His earlier exploration of the Mississippi basin had underpinned France's claim to Louisiana.

events.title: David Livingstone Is Born
events.description: The Scottish missionary and explorer was born in Blantyre, Scotland. He rose from work in a cotton mill to become one of Victorian Britain's best-known figures.
events.significance: Livingstone's journeys across southern and central Africa reshaped European maps of the continent. His campaigning against the slave trade also shaped public opinion.

events.title: The Lumière Brothers Film Their First Footage
events.description: Auguste and Louis Lumière shot their first motion-picture footage, a short scene of workers leaving their family's factory in Lyon, France.
events.significance: The film was an early step toward cinema as a public entertainment. The brothers' projected shows later that year helped launch the movie industry.

events.title: The First International Women's Day
events.description: More than a million people in Austria, Denmark, Germany and Switzerland joined rallies for women's rights. The idea came from activists including Clara Zetkin and Luise Zietz.
events.significance: The event started a tradition that now unfolds worldwide every year. It is now observed each March 8.

events.title: Nevada Legalizes Gambling
events.description: Nevada's governor signed a bill making casino gambling legal across the state. Lawmakers hoped it would bring in revenue during the Great Depression.
events.significance: The decision laid the groundwork for Las Vegas and Reno to become gambling destinations. It also made tourism and entertainment central to Nevada's economy.
